transcript.text: Sometimes when I open the dishwasher there's grey smelly water in the bottom even though it finished draining fine. Not every day though. Kitchen sink was replaced last month if that matters.

Yes, the sink replacement could be relevant. Because the dishwasher appears to finish its drain but dirty, smelly water is only there sometimes afterwards, the leading possibility is dirty water flowing back from the sink waste into the dishwasher. A partial blockage in the dishwasher filter/sump or drain hose is the next possibility. 1. With the dishwasher switched off and unplugged, remove and clean the bottom filter. Wipe or rinse away grease and food debris, and check the sump beneath for anything obvious such as glass or labels. A dirty filter can slow the final drain and cause smells. 2. Under the sink, run the tap and see whether the sink drains freely, without gurgling or rising water. Then check the dishwasher’s grey drain hose is not squashed or kinked behind the machine or under the sink. Slow sink drainage or a kink supports a waste/drainage restriction. 3. Look where that hose joins the new sink waste. The hose should be firmly attached and routed up as high as practical under the worktop before dropping to the waste connection; this high loop helps prevent sink water running back. If the new waste fitting has a dishwasher spigot, make sure it is actually open rather than still blanked off. If the filter and hose route are clear but this keeps happening, the sink trap/waste connection may need the installer or a plumber to revisit, particularly as the timing matches the sink work. If the plumbing is most likely sound, a sticking dishwasher non-return valve or a partial internal drain blockage becomes more likely.

I checked under the sink. Since the new sink went in the hose just lies on the cupboard floor and goes straight into the waste spigot, no high loop. The filter is clean though, and the sink drains a little slow. The water seems to appear after I drain the sink full of washing-up water.

This is very strongly pointing to sink water backing into the dishwasher, rather than the dishwasher failing to drain. The decisive clue is that it appears after emptying a full sink of washing-up water, and the hose has been left low on the cupboard floor with no high loop. The sink fitter or a plumber should:
1. Clear/check the slow-draining sink trap and waste pipework.
2. Re-route the dishwasher drain hose up as high as practical beneath the worktop, securely clipped, before it drops down to the waste spigot. This is the high loop that prevents dirty sink water running back.
3. Check the waste spigot connection is secure and unrestricted. A clean dishwasher filter makes an internal dishwasher blockage less likely. A sticking dishwasher non-return valve is possible, but only becomes a serious suspect if the water still returns after the sink waste is draining freely and the hose has been correctly high-looped. Until it is altered, avoid emptying a full sink quickly where possible, and remove any returned water from the dishwasher before running it. The smelly water is contaminated sink waste, so run a hot empty dishwasher-cleaner cycle after the plumbing issue is corrected.

candidates: Sink waste connection allowing dirty water to run back into the dishwasher (high)
Partial blockage in the dishwasher filter, sump or drain hose (medium)

reading.symptom: Sometimes grey smelly water is in the bottom after a cycle

plan: The fault they reported is: "Sometimes grey smelly water is in the bottom after a cycle". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.

candidates: Sink waste water backing up through an incorrectly routed dishwasher drain hose (high)
Partial blockage or restriction in the new sink waste/trap (medium)
